question: Can a Transformer language model be made robust at out-of-distribution algorithmic reasoning by letting its tokens cross-attend to embeddings from a pre-trained GNN-based neural algorithmic reasoner?
hypothesis: Uniting Transformers with NARs leads to fruitful returns on both sides: NAR embeddings make the Transformer more robust out of distribution.
contributions: A hybrid architecture (TransNAR) combining a Transformer's language understanding with a pre-trained GNN-based NAR, which the Transformer uses as a high-dimensional tool that modulates its token embeddings.
An evaluation on CLRS-Text showing improved and more robust OOD reasoning versus Transformer-only baselines.

method.summary: A 70M decoder-only Chinchilla-family Transformer has gated cross-attention layers interleaved (Flamingo style) that attend to node and edge embeddings of a frozen, pre-trained Triplet-GMPNN NAR run on the graph version of the same problem. Trained with next-token prediction on CLRS-Text problem sizes 4-8 and 12, evaluated on sizes 10, 12 and 14.
method.task: algorithmic reasoning in text (CLRS-Text, 30 CLRS algorithms), size generalisation

datasets.name: CLRS-Text
datasets.size: 10,000 samples per algorithm per input size; 2,400,000 data points total
datasets.split: 70% train / 30% validation; train sizes [4, 8] and 12; eval sizes 10 (OOD interpolation), 12 (in-distribution), 14 (OOD extrapolation)
datasets.source: Markeeva et al. 2024, text version of CLRS-30 derived deterministically from the graph version
datasets.preprocessing: Text and graph versions carry identical information; randomized positional encoding max length 8,192 on top of RoPE

models.name: TransNAR
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer with interleaved gated cross-attention to frozen NAR node and edge embeddings
models.init_from: two variants: Pretrained (Chinchilla 70M pretrained on MassiveText) and Untrained (random init)

other.node_edge_combination: concatenate node and edge cross-attention outputs then a linear layer; sum, 2-layer MLP and Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation gave no improvement
other.edge_flattening: edge features E in R^{NxNxk} flattened over first two axes

models.name: NAR (Triplet-GMPNN)
models.architecture: multi-task Triplet-GMPNN with triplet interactions and gating, shared function per step, frozen during TransNAR training
models.init_from: pre-trained on CLRS-30, sizes up to 16, following Ibarz et al. 2022

models.name: Transformer baseline
models.architecture: same Chinchilla decoder-only 6-layer model, no NAR, with randomized positional encoding; Pretrained and Untrained variants

training.epochs: seven epochs of the training data
training.regularisation: randomized positional encoding (max length 8,192) on top of RoPE

other.nar_frozen: NAR parameters frozen during fine-tuning to preserve robustness

inference.samples: 4 random seeds per model; error bars +-1 std
inference.prompting: CLRS-Text format, e.g. 'binary search: key: [...], target: 0.122 return: 2'; no prompt modification or tool use

metrics.name: CLRS score
metrics.definition: percentage of elements in the output matching ground truth; 0 if shape score is 0

metrics.name: Shape score
metrics.definition: binary: output has the right shape for input and task

metrics.name: Parse score
metrics.definition: binary: output free of illicit characters

baselines: Transformer-only Chinchilla 70M, Pretrained and Untrained, with randomized positional encoding
eval.protocol: Per-algorithm scores over 8 algorithm families at sizes 10, 12, 14; 4 seeds, +-1 std error bars. Exact string match deliberately not used.

evidence.quote: We train all models over seven epochs of the training data with a batch size of 256

results.claim: TransNAR gives over 20% absolute OOD improvement on several algorithm classes versus the Transformer baseline.
results.setup: CLRS-Text, 70M Chinchilla Transformer vs TransNAR, OOD sizes (Figure 1 caption)
results.note: Only a threshold is stated; per-algorithm numbers are in Fig 4, not in text.

results.claim: TransNAR significantly outperforms the baseline overall and on most algorithms, in and out of distribution, and makes capabilities emerge where the baseline scored zero or near-zero.
TransNAR raises the share of outputs with correct shape OOD, a main failure mode of the plain Transformer, though not always to perfect scores.
TransNAR does not beat the baseline on Binary Search, Find Maximum Subarray, Minimum and Quickselect, all index-search tasks.
Randomized positional encoding helped both models; without it the hybrid was capped by a near-zero base LLM.

limits: Requires both text and graph inputs, so only usable where a ground-truth executor or simulator exists (Sec 4.2).
Authors suggest distilling TransNAR into a vanilla Transformer to remove the second stream; not done.
Parse score: TransNAR falls behind baseline on a few algorithms in extrapolation, attributed to insufficient cross-attention capacity (Fig 6).
Only a 70M model, sizes up to 14; no results in text as numbers (all in figures); no compute, hardware, schedule or code stated.
Search-index tasks failed to generalise to unseen index boundaries; index hints proposed but not tested.

terms.definition: neural algorithmic reasoner: GNN-based system trained as a generic solver for algorithmic tasks in graph form

lineage.work: The CLRS-Text algorithmic reasoning language benchmark
Randomized positional encodings boost length generalization of transformers
